content.text: : I am not able to reproduce this error using the same versions of the Fedora server and Import/Export utility. The only difference in my setup is that I am not using the "–writeConfig" option.
Also, I see that your error message indicates a data directory (data-export-versioned-binaries) which is different from the data directory listed in your import command (export).

:  hmmm,  interesting.  I'll try it again.  The data direct is not an issue.  I forgot to  update the data directory in the error message to reflect the "export" dir I used in the command.  In fact I used /Users/danny/import-export-sprint-3/data-export-versioned-binaries for invoking the command, but I changed it in the example to simplify.
, I was just noting the discrepancy in data directories as a possible indication that the test documented in the ticket description may have been run in an inconsistent environment.
In using the latest on the master branch of the import export tool ( ie  4a97b2)
I'm still seeing the same error on the import side, but the import appears to have succeeded.  The import did not report a failure:  only two errors:
ERROR 14:58:12.670 (Importer) Error while importing /Users/danny/import-export-sprint-3/fcrepo-2504/f4/rest/test.ttl (409): Could not persist triple containing predicate

ERROR 14:58:13.075 (Importer) Error while importing /Users/danny/import-export-sprint-3/fcrepo-2504/f4/rest/test/90/2a/c8/ef/902ac8ef-3ebe-4b00-ab05-87e54d2db0e8/fcr%3Ametadata.ttl (409): Could not persist triple containing predicate
: are you running your fcrepo-webapp-4.8.0-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console-a07a1a46.jar with the {{-Dfcrepo.properties.management="relaxed"}} option?
That option allows for overwriting some of the server-managed triples... include
:  I will try it with the relax option enabled.
With relaxed option enabled, I don't see the error.  I will close the issue.

comments.body:
Danny Bernstein: I am not able to reproduce this error using the same versions of the Fedora server and Import/Export utility. The only difference in my setup is that I am not using the "–writeConfig" option.

Also, I see that your error message indicates a data directory (data-export-versioned-binaries) which is different from the data directory listed in your import command (export).

Andrew Woods:  hmmm,  interesting.  I'll try it again.  The data direct is not an issue.  I forgot to  update the data directory in the error message to reflect the "export" dir I used in the command.  In fact I used /Users/danny/import-export-sprint-3/data-export-versioned-binaries for invoking the command, but I changed it in the example to simplify.
Danny Bernstein, I was just noting the discrepancy in data directories as a possible indication that the test documented in the ticket description may have been run in an inconsistent environment.

In using the latest on the master branch of the import export tool ( ie  4a97b2) 

I'm still seeing the same error on the import side, but the import appears to have succeeded.  The import did not report a failure:  only two errors:

 

ERROR 14:58:12.670 (Importer) Error while importing /Users/danny/import-export-sprint-3/fcrepo-2504/f4/rest/test.ttl (409): Could not persist triple containing predicate http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#lastModifiedBy to node /test
ERROR 14:58:13.075 (Importer) Error while importing /Users/danny/import-export-sprint-3/fcrepo-2504/f4/rest/test/90/2a/c8/ef/902ac8ef-3ebe-4b00-ab05-87e54d2db0e8/fcr%3Ametadata.ttl (409): Could not persist triple containing predicate http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#lastModifiedBy to node /test/90/2a/c8/ef/902ac8ef-3ebe-4b00-ab05-87e54d2db0e8/jcr:content

Danny Bernstein: are you running your fcrepo-webapp-4.8.0-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console-a07a1a46.jar with the -Dfcrepo.properties.management="relaxed" option?

That option allows for overwriting some of the server-managed triples... include lastModifiedBy.
Andrew Woods:  I will try it with the relax option enabled.
With relaxed option enabled, I don't see the error.  I will close the issue.
